blocks.text:
The sightseeing day takes 8 hours, including transfers.

Altitude: 2,800 m.

Average temperature: +20 °C during the day and +10 °C at night.

On your Quito city tour, you’ll take in city views and see historic churches, domes and rooftops. Along the way, you’ll learn about colonial art, architecture and culture, as well as local legends and traditions.

Quito, the capital of Ecuador, was founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city and sits at an altitude of 2,800 m. Its historic centre retains its colonial architecture. The buildings and their richly decorated interiors showcase the Quito School, which brought together Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous artistic traditions. Its artists carved stone and wood to depict major religious events. A 90-minute walk through the Old Town shows why Quito’s historic centre was placed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

Quito takes its name from the Quitu people, who inhabited the region long before the Spanish conquest. Sebastián de Benalcázar took control of the city in 1533. It had served as a capital of the Inca Empire and was granted the status of a Spanish city in 1541. Its full name is San Francisco de Quito. It remained the capital of the territory of Quito until the end of Spanish colonial rule.

The Franciscans were the first religious order to establish themselves in Quito. They immediately began building a monastery, which became a centre for education and the arts, with its own schools of painting and sculpture.

Around the main square, Plaza Grande, stand the Metropolitan Cathedral, the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop’s Palace and City Hall. We’ll visit the Jesuit church, an outstanding example of the city’s colonial art, with intricate carvings covering its façade.

We’ll also visit the Gothic Basílica del Voto Nacional. Its French architect drew inspiration from Notre-Dame de Paris. The basilica is considered Ecuador’s foremost example of Neo-Gothic architecture and one of the most notable in Latin America.

Established in the 19th century, the basilica is considered unfinished. Its façade features gargoyles and figures of animals native to Ecuador and the region, including caimans, turtles, boobies and monkeys.

The church is 140 m long and 35 m wide, with a central nave 30 m high. Its two front towers are 115 m high, making the basilica one of the tallest structures in Quito.

Quito is a capital of contrasts, as you’ll see when you visit the Old Town and newer districts. From the El Panecillo viewpoint, where a winged statue of the Virgin Mary, the city’s patroness, stands, you’ll have a view across the city.

Next we’ll head to the Middle of the World, where we’ll visit two sites associated with the equator:

1) Ciudad Mitad del Mundo

This visitor complex is home to a monument commemorating the 1736 geodetic expedition that identified this spot as the equator. Managed by the government of Pichincha Province, the complex lies in San Antonio parish in the Metropolitan District of Quito, north of the city centre.

The 30 m monument was built between 1979 and 1982 to mark where the equator was believed to run. A line extending from the centre of the monument marks the presumed equator, and countless visitors have stepped across it over the years. The entire structure stands 240 m south of the actual equator, whose position was determined more accurately in the 20th century with GPS.

2) Intiñan Museum

At the museum, you can try several activities presented as demonstrations linked to the equator, including watching water swirl, balancing a chicken egg and walking along the equator line. You’ll also learn about ancient cultures and the tsantsa ritual and see totems from several South American cultures. The grounds include examples of traditional dwellings from different cultures in Ecuador, including a house with belongings from an Indigenous family that lived there many generations ago.

Stops: Basílica del Voto Nacional, Plaza Grande, the Golden Church, Plaza de San Francisco, the hill with the statue of the Virgin Mary, Intiñan Museum and Mitad del Mundo.

Return to the hotel. Evening at leisure.
